findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category was never customized
findings.body: When the legacy embed_category setting has no row in site_settings (the common case where the default '' was never overridden) or its named category no longer exists, the JOIN returns zero rows and execute(...)[0] is nil, so ['id'] raises NoMethodError. The intended `if category_id == 0` fallback is never reached, blocking the upgrade; the uncategorized fallback lookup on line 15 has the same unguarded [0] pattern.

findings.title: Migration stores legacy hosts verbatim so prefixed hosts stop matching
findings.body: Legacy embeddable_hosts values could contain entries such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (the old SiteSetting matcher stripped scheme/path). This raw-SQL INSERT bypasses EmbeddableHost's before_validation trimming, so the stored host remains the full URL while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against only URI(url).host ('discourse.org'); such migrated hosts will silently stop being allowed after the upgrade until manually re-saved. The unescaped '#{h}' interpolation also breaks the INSERT if a legacy value contains a single quote.

findings.title: Update/destroy return 500 for a stale or nonexistent host id
findings.body: update and destroy assign host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first, which is nil for an unknown or already-deleted id, and then call save_host(host)/host.destroy on nil. Concurrent admins deleting/editing the same row (or a stale client) therefore get a NoMethodError 500 instead of a 404/JSON error.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation
findings.body: The callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!. If create/update is called without a host key, the controller assigns nil and validation raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 rather than the render_json_error 422 path that a blank/invalid host should take.

findings.title: Hosts with an explicit port can be saved but never match
findings.body: The format validation on line 2 explicitly permits a port suffix (e.g. 'example.com:8080'), and before_validation strips only scheme and path, so such a host is stored with its port. record_for_host then extracts uri.host, which drops the port, and compares it to the stored 'example.com:8080', so host_allowed? is always false for a host the admin UI accepted.

findings.title: Edit crashes when a host has no resolvable category
findings.body: The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') without a guard. When category_id is dangling (category deleted) or hydration could not resolve the category, host.category is undefined and clicking edit throws a TypeError, making that row impossible to fix from the UI. The save path has the related issue of setting host.category from Category.findById(null) when no category is chosen, even though the server defaults a blank category_id to the uncategorized category.

findings.title: Plural embedded hydration replaces missing records with undefined and discards the ids
findings.body: For *_ids keys the new code unconditionally maps each id through _lookupSubType, assigns the result to the plural property, and deletes the original *_ids key. Unlike the singular branch (which preserves the id when nothing is found), if the root payload lacks the side-loaded collection or omits one record, the property becomes an array containing undefined entries and the original ids are lost, so consumers iterating the collection (e.g. embedding's embeddable_hosts) hit undefined objects instead of knowing which ids were referenced.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint on embeddable host names
findings.body: The table has no unique index on host and EmbeddableHost validates only the host format, so the same host (including case variants like 'Example.com' vs 'example.com', which record_for_host matches case-insensitively) can be created multiple times with different categories. record_for_host then returns .first with no ordering, making the category chosen for embedded topics from that host arbitrary.

findings.title: Category and embeddable-host fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the new spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators. Tests still pass only because all fabricator files are loaded together; the swapped names mislead future edits and deleting or modifying the 'embeddable host' fabricator file would actually remove the category fabricators used across the suite.
